purpose: Fluvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and triglycerides (fats) in your blood. It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart problems. Your doctor may prescribe it along with a healthy diet and lifestyle changes.
how_it_works: Your liver naturally makes cholesterol, but sometimes it makes too much. Fluvastatin works by blocking a key enzyme in your liver called HMG-CoA reductase, which is responsible for producing cholesterol. By slowing down cholesterol production, the drug helps lower the bad cholesterol (LDL) in your blood and can raise the good cholesterol (HDL).
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well, but some may experience muscle aches or weakness, headache, stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, or mild joint pain. These side effects are usually mild and often go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have severe muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark-colored urine, as this could be a rare but serious condition called rhabdomyolysis. Do not take fluvastatin if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it can harm your baby. Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice and tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with this drug. Your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests periodically.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 20 to 40 mg taken once a day in the evening. Your doctor may increase the dose up to 80 mg per day depending on your cholesterol levels. The extended-release tablet (Lescol XL 80 mg) is taken once daily at any time of day. Always take it as your doctor prescribes and do not stop without talking to them first.
